revenue_model: Revenue is driven by gross merchandise value (GMV) from selling finished goods to end consumers, measured in units sold × average selling price (ASP), with no production or conversion of raw materials.
notes: Retail & E-Commerce does not manufacture goods; it procures finished goods from suppliers and sells them, so installed capacity, capacity utilisation, raw-material holding, and finished-goods holding (as a production metric) are meaningless.
Cost of goods sold (COGS) is the purchase price of inventory, not per-unit conversion costs; there are no cost1/cost2 per unit in a manufacturing sense.
Fixed assets are primarily warehouses, IT infrastructure, and leasehold improvements; plant & machinery is rare unless the business owns packaging or fulfilment automation equipment.

Working capital is dominated by inventory holding (days of stock cover) and payment cycles with suppliers and payment gateways, not raw-material or finished-goods holding days from a factory perspective.

term_loan_amount.label: Term Loan Amount (INR)
term_loan_amount.rationale: Retail & E-Commerce businesses borrow for warehouse setup, technology, and expansion; amounts vary widely by scale.

promoters_capital.label: Promoters' Capital / Equity (INR)
promoters_capital.rationale: Minimum promoter contribution typically 20-25% of project cost as per RBI norms for retail trade.

interest_rate_term_loan.label: Term Loan Interest Rate (p.a.)
interest_rate_term_loan.rationale: Banks charge 9-14% for retail trade term loans depending on credit profile and collateral.

term_loan_tenure_months.label: Term Loan Tenure (months)
term_loan_tenure_months.rationale: Typical tenure for retail term loans is 3-7 years, with 5 years being common.

moratorium_months.label: Moratorium / Grace Period (months)
moratorium_months.rationale: Moratorium of 0-6 months is allowed for retail projects before principal repayment begins.

interest_rate_wc.label: Working Capital Interest Rate (p.a.)
interest_rate_wc.rationale: Working capital loans for retail carry 10-15% interest, often linked to MCLR plus spread.

income_tax_rate.label: Effective Income Tax Rate (corporate)
income_tax_rate.rationale: Indian companies pay 25-30% effective tax including surcharge and cess; retail businesses usually opt for lower rate if eligible.

installed_capacity.rationale: Retail & E-Commerce has no installed capacity in a manufacturing sense; there are no production machines or production lines.

capacity_utilisation_y1_y5.rationale: Capacity utilisation is a factory concept; retail businesses measure store footfall or website traffic, not machine utilisation.

monthly_seasonality_weights.label: Monthly Seasonality Weights (sales multiplier)
monthly_seasonality_weights.rationale: Retail sales are highly seasonal — festive months (Diwali, wedding season) peak 1.5-1.8x, lean months (Feb, March) dip to 0.6-0.8x.

selling_price_y1.label: Average Selling Price (ASP) per unit (INR)
selling_price_y1.rationale: ASP varies hugely by category; grocery items ~100-500 INR, electronics/apparel 1000-10000 INR.

selling_price_escalation.label: Annual ASP Escalation (%)
selling_price_escalation.rationale: ASP escalation tracks inflation and brand premium; typically 2-6% p.a. for retail, not cost-driven escalation.

cost1_per_unit_y1.rationale: Cost1 per unit implies a direct material cost in production; retail COGS is the purchase price of finished goods, not a per-unit conversion cost.

cost1_escalation.rationale: No cost1 exists; inventory purchase price escalation is captured in gross margin compression, not a separate cost line.

cost2_per_unit_y1.rationale: Cost2 per unit (e.g., labour or overhead per unit) is meaningless in retail where costs are period costs, not unit-linked.

cost2_escalation.rationale: No cost2 per unit to escalate; retail overheads are period costs, not variable per unit of sale.

other_variable_cost_y1.label: Other Variable Costs (e.g., payment gateway, packaging) per unit (INR)
other_variable_cost_y1.rationale: E-Commerce includes payment gateway fees (~2% of GMV), packaging costs (5-20 INR/unit), and delivery charges (if not passed to customer).

other_variable_escalation.label: Other Variable Cost Escalation (%)
other_variable_escalation.rationale: These costs escalate with inflation and logistics cost increases; typically 3-7% p.a.

wages_monthly_y1.label: Total Employee Cost (monthly, INR)
wages_monthly_y1.rationale: Includes store staff, warehouse workers, and corporate team; ranges from small store (~50K) to large e-commerce (~50L monthly).

wages_escalation.label: Employee Cost Escalation (%)
wages_escalation.rationale: Wages in retail grow 5-10% p.a. due to inflation, minimum wage hikes, and attrition.

factory_overheads_monthly_y1.rationale: Factory overheads do not exist in retail; the equivalent is warehouse/fulfilment centre overheads, captured under admin or selling expenses.

factory_oh_escalation.rationale: No factory overhead to escalate; warehouse costs are part of selling & distribution or admin.

repairs_maintenance_monthly_y1.label: Repairs & Maintenance (monthly, INR)
repairs_maintenance_monthly_y1.rationale: Covers store/warehouse upkeep, IT hardware, and fixtures; typically 0.5-2% of fixed asset value annually.

rm_escalation.label: Repairs & Maintenance Escalation (%)
rm_escalation.rationale: R&M costs escalate with inflation and asset age; 3-6% p.a. is typical.

admin_expenses_monthly_y1.label: Administrative & General Expenses (monthly, INR)
admin_expenses_monthly_y1.rationale: Includes rent (if not separate), utilities, office supplies, professional fees; varies with scale.

admin_escalation.label: Admin Expense Escalation (%)
admin_escalation.rationale: Admin expenses grow with inflation and business expansion; 4-8% p.a. is common.

selling_distribution.label: Selling & Distribution Expenses (% of sales)
selling_distribution.rationale: Includes marketing, logistics, and fulfilment; 2-10% of GMV for retail, higher for e-commerce (5-10%).

land_cost.label: Land Cost (INR)
land_cost.rationale: Many retail businesses lease premises; land cost is zero for leased operations, but can be significant for owned stores/warehouses.

building_cost.label: Building / Warehouse / Store Construction Cost (INR)
building_cost.rationale: Cost of constructing or fitting out a retail store or warehouse; ranges from 50L for small store to 20Cr for large fulfilment centre.

building_dep_rate.label: Building Depreciation Rate (%)
building_dep_rate.rationale: Buildings depreciate at 5-10% p.a. under WDV as per Companies Act; retail warehouses use 10%.

plant_machinery_cost.rationale: Retail & E-Commerce rarely owns plant & machinery; equipment like conveyors or sorters in fulfilment centres is classified as furniture or IT assets.

plant_machinery_dep_rate.rationale: No plant & machinery to depreciate; if automation exists, it is depreciated under furniture or IT at 15-20%.

furniture_other_cost.label: Furniture, Fixtures, IT & Equipment Cost (INR)
furniture_other_cost.rationale: Includes store shelving, POS systems, computers, servers; typically 2-10 lakh per store, higher for e-commerce tech stack.

furniture_dep_rate.label: Furniture & IT Depreciation Rate (%)
furniture_dep_rate.rationale: Furniture depreciates at 10-15%, IT equipment at 15-20% p.a. under WDV.

raw_material_holding_days.rationale: Retail does not hold raw materials; it holds finished goods inventory purchased from suppliers.

finished_goods_holding_days.rationale: This field is meant for manufacturing finished goods; retail holds inventory (stock cover) measured in days of sales, not days of production.

receivables_days.label: Receivables / Debtor Days (days)
receivables_days.rationale: Retail sales are mostly cash or card; e-commerce receives payment in 1-7 days from payment gateways; B2B retail can have 15 days. Very low vs manufacturing.

payables_days.label: Payables / Creditor Days (days)
payables_days.rationale: Retailers get 15-60 days credit from suppliers, with 30 days being typical for fast-moving goods.

min_cash_balance.label: Minimum Cash / Bank Balance (INR)
min_cash_balance.rationale: Retail needs cash for daily operations, petty cash, and unforeseen expenses; 5-10% of monthly sales is common.

wc_margin_pct.label: Working Capital Margin / Promoter Contribution (%)
wc_margin_pct.rationale: Banks require 20-25% margin on working capital limit as per RBI guidelines for retail trade.
